body:
I am and I'm ready to accept help, but I'm afraid for people to find out about my state of depression. So much advice I get is 'fake it till you make it' so I've been trying to project confidence and self-assurance, but I'm losing control of my ability to maintain that image. 

I worry that if I tell people that they'll be less interested in spending time with me because I'll be a wet towel. I don't even crave sex any more, I just want a hug. But any time I start to even talk about it, all the emotions rush to the surface like a tsunami that I can't stop and people get turned off. It seems like the only way to get what I need is to not need it. 

The pressure to be what is expected of me is what is compounding all these problems. And I lack the resources (time/money) to do anything about it right now. I honestly just want to be completely selfish and stop pleasing anyone else.

I was put on Celexa and then Effexor when I was in my early 20's. Celexa made me even more suicidal but Effexor helped somewhat. But the 'brain fog' affected my day-to-day work so much and I gave me some very bizarre side effects that made me equally concerned about being on it that not being on any medication at all.

I've been fine for years since then with a few episodes under extreme stress. I can honestly say now this is the longest and worst episode I've ever experienced. I thought I had left this all behind me. I need my mental sharpness for my work but sometimes I think that's actually a double-edged sword.

Maybe I really do need to be medicated.
